issues: scripts/run_accounting_master.py — Master.execute_phase resets the deletion baseline before every repair. If implementation deletes a pre-existing tracked file, changes_since detects it and raises MasterError. The next repair snapshots the already-damaged tree, so leaving that file absent no longer appears in changes['deleted']. Passing checks and AGREE can then accept the phase without restoring the prohibited deletion. A worker returning BLOCKED bypasses changes_since entirely, creating the same risk on resume. Preserve a durable phase-entry inventory and byte references across retries and resumed attempts; reconcile deletions after every editable worker outcome, including BLOCKED and handled failures. Require restoration of every outstanding prohibited deletion before acceptance. Keep cumulative changes available to the reviewer as well as the latest repair delta.

scripts/run_accounting_master.py — Master.execute_phase handles BLOCKED only from plan and implementation/repair workers. A BLOCKED plan review is treated as a request for plan repair; a BLOCKED result review triggers another editable repair. Exhaustion becomes needs_plan_repair or needs_repair rather than blocked_external, defeating the stated rule that unchanged external blocks are skipped and potentially repeating work against an unavailable prerequisite. Handle BLOCKED explicitly after both review calls, preserve its issues and residuals, and use the existing external-block tracking path. If review roles cannot emit BLOCKED, that missing interface restriction must be stated and an explicit supported mechanism must convey external blockers discovered during review.
next_actions: Add regression coverage for deletion followed by an otherwise successful repair, and deletion followed by BLOCKED and resume; acceptance must remain impossible until restoration.
